column1: What are the three inputs and two outputs of a full adder?
column2: Inputs: two operand bits and a carry-in. Outputs: sum and carry-out.

column1: How many NAND gates does a full adder require?

column2: A chain of full adders in which the carry-out of bit i feeds the carry-in of bit i+1; the answer ripples through bit by bit.
Arithmetic Logic Unit — the collection of adders, subtractors, shifters, bitwise logic units, and comparators that does a CPU’s arithmetic in one clock cycle.

column1: What is an SR latch built from?
column2: Two cross-coupled NAND gates — each gate’s output feeds the other gate’s input.

column1: How many transistors does an SR latch use in CMOS?
column2: Eight — four transistors per NAND gate, two gates.

column2: They live next to the ALU, are built from cross-coupled NANDs, and are accessed in a single clock cycle — a third of a nanosecond at 3 GHz.
